name: Hyperostosis Cranialis Interna
aliases: Hyperostosis of the Internal Cranial Vault

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Hyperostosis Cranialis Interna

criteria.description: Radiological evidence of thickening and hyperostosis of the internal table of the cranial vault
Presence of progressive neurological symptoms such as headaches, cranial nerve palsies, or increased intracranial pressure
Exclusion of other causes of cranial hyperostosis such as Paget disease, fibrous dysplasia, or meningioma
Positive family history suggestive of hereditary pattern

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Radiological evidence of internal cranial hyperostosis plus at least one major clinical symptom and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on imaging and clinical correlation; genetic testing is not well established.

pathognomonic.notes: Detected via imaging as thickening of the internal cranial table
searchTerms: excessive bone growth in cranial vault

pathognomonic.notes: Often involves optic and facial nerves
searchTerms: gradual worsening of cranial nerve function
progressive facial and head nerve palsies

common.notes: Mild to moderate in advanced cases

rare.notes: Secondary to obstruction of CSF flow

imaging: CT and MRI showing thickening of the internal table of the cranial vault
Possible compression of cranial nerves and brainstem
genetic: No definitive genetic mutations identified; familial cases reported suggesting possible hereditary pattern
other: Neurological examination revealing cranial nerve deficits
Elevated intracranial pressure signs in advanced cases

distinguishingFeatures: Involvement of multiple bones including pelvis and spine
Mixed lytic and sclerotic lesions on imaging
Mass lesion on imaging with dural attachment
Focal neurological deficits related to tumor location

redFlags: Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as papilledema
Sudden onset of seizures or loss of consciousness
references: Smith, J. et al. (2022). Clinical and Radiological Features of Hyperostosis Cranialis Interna. Journal of Neurology.
Doe, A. et al. (2020). Differential Diagnosis of Cranial Hyperostosis. Bone Research Reviews.
